question: Does a newly valid checkpoint truncate useful refinement through its effect on rollback, independently of image preparation, gradients and physical acceptance rules?

arms.current: Existing fallback tracks the latest valid checkpoint; failed blocks roll back.
arms.best-safe: Fallback tracks the best valid checkpoint, while acceptance and continuing exploration are otherwise unchanged.
arms.improving: Only a checkpoint preferred by the existing objective becomes the next accepted trajectory checkpoint. Worse valid checkpoints cause fallback to the best valid state. All original geometry and paper gates remain.
arms.no-rollback: Diagnostic only: continue gradient exploration through failed checkpoints, while still returning the best validated incumbent and retaining unresolved alternatives. Never accepts an invalid state as a valid export.

cases.name: bird
cases.input: Captured first feature-detail plan from the x+1 photograph: identical initial controls, weights and probability, 160 steps.

cases.input: Frozen photographed crop and initial curves; 750 fixed refinement steps.

cases.input: Frozen photographed crop and initial curves; 81 steps.

controls: No crop, classified-mask, probability, weight, tolerance, count, gradient or initial-curve changes.
Current production copied to an isolated runtime, with a separate refine implementation per arm. Runtime, harness, shared helpers and fixture hashes checked before and after each run.
Twenty fits run serially only after QA reaches a terminal state. Missing QA handle without terminal state stops the queue; it never restarts the QA job.
Each returned candidate is saved before independent validation. Record actual computed steps as well as requested work because cycle skipping can differ.
measurements: Independent exported mask disagreement and enclosed-feature component shape.
Original and finer actual paper lattices at 700 and 1000, plus independent polygon-offset final verification.
Geometry validity, retained uncertain/failed alternatives, checkpoint history, and repeated-rollback behavior.
Bird rejected checkpoints saved for subsequent routing comparisons; this fixed-plan study alone cannot establish fresh end-to-end success.
acceptance: Do not integrate an arm merely because it restores a historical hash or closes an inflated eye. Require the original geometry/paper gates and feature quality, then fresh timed end-to-end corpus comparisons.
